text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - General Motors Corp is expected to announce a sponsorship agreement with General Electric's NBC and the United States Olympic Committee that would run into the next decade and be worth several hundred million dollars, the New York Times reports.

PARIS - Havas Advertising, the French advertising group, has forged a link with a French rugby club that experts say shows the growing importance of sports sponsorship. Havas Advertising chairman Alain de Pouzhilac says the company is working with rugby club Racing Club Narbone on strategy, promotion, marketing, merchandising, advertising and public relations.

LONDON - JWT Europe, part of the WPP Group Plc's J. Walter Thompson advertising agency, says it is expanding into Ukraine via an agreement with Ark Communications. JWT has formed an affiliation with Ark Communications in Kiev, with the possibility of gaining equity in the operation later this year.

PARIS - Canal J, a French television channel for children available only on cable or satellite networks, says it is running its first advertising campaign on terrestrial television from August 2 to August 10.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Recently floated television group ProSieben Media AG says chief editor Gerd Berger is leaving the company, and it will reduce the amount of in-house productions aired on its channels. ProSieben, which runs the ProSieben and Kabel 1 cable TV channels, says Jan Koerbelin would take responsibility for all output.

NEW YORK - Americans will spend an average of $546 this year on media and entertainment, ranging from movies to music to computer online services, up 6 percent from 1996, according to a new survey. The same growth is expected next year, rising to an average of $583, and spending will increase to an estimated $685 by the year 2001, says media investment banking firm Veronis, Suhler & Associates Inc.

HONG KONG - Turner International says it has reached an agreement with pay television provider Austar to expand distribution of the TNT & Cartoon Network in Australia. The agreement, effective August 1, will provide programming to another 150,000 subscribers.

LONDON - Britain's Department of Trade & Industry says the current government funding formula used to run Channel 4 would end from 1999, because Channel 4's success means the system is no longer needed. Designed as a system of income support for state-owned Channel 4, the success of the channel has meant that the ITV commercial television companies have been receiving hefty annual payments from C4.

KATHMANDU - Nepal plans to privatise a state-owned telecommunications company and a publishing house, Finance Minister Rabindra Nath Sharma says. The Telecommunications Corp, a telecommunications monopoly, and Gorkhapatra Corp, publisher of two daily newspapers as well as four other publications, will be studied for privatisation," Sharma tells parliament.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

CHICAGO - Another "impulse" offering is being added to the checkout lines at about 35 Wal-Mart stores across the U.S. -- McDonald's Extra Value Meals. In addition to candy, gum, breath mints, horoscope books and magazines, customers can buy the Extra Value Meals -- consisting of a sandwich, french fries and a drink -- and pay for them at the Wal-Mart checkout.

LONDON - The Body Shop, the retailer which markets itself with high-profile environmental campaigns, hopes new-style stores offering massages, manicures and facials will put some pep back into its sales. The Body Shop, which has evolved into an international retailer since its founding in England 21 years ago, has been experiencing stagnating sales in Britian and falling sales in the U.S. and Asia.

NEW YORK - Leading record companies and consumer electronics manufacturers have agreed on the broad technical guidelines for digital video disc (DVD) audio format, which the recording industry has decided to introduce as a replacement for compact disks, The New York Times reports. The paper says the accord signals a fundamental shift in the recorded music business, away from two-channel stereo sound to multi-channel audio, using six speakers.

BUDAPEST - Volkswagen AG continued to widen its lead in central Europe's booming market for new cars in May, while Daewoo Group overtook Fiat SPA for second place, according to a monthly Reuters survey. "Volkswagen is a step ahead of Daewoo and Fiat -- its products are technically superior," auto analyst Vic Heylen says.

OAK BROOK, Illinois - McDonald's Corp and Walt Disney Co say they have extended their marketing alliance to include more co-branding activities. As part of the new program, two McDonald's restaurants will open in Walt Disney World Resort in Florida and another restaurant will open at Disneyland Paris. McDonald's will also sponsor the Dinoland USA section of Disney's Animal Kingdom theme park in Florida, opening in spring 1998.

BEIJING - China will set up its biggest compact disc production base in the southern province of Guangdong as part of efforts to crack down on piracy, officials say. The project would have the capacity to produce 40 million compact discs, video compact discs and CD-ROMs a year after it goes into operation, an official of the Guangdong Press and Publications Administration says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - The worldwide personal computer market had a robust second quarter, with shipments up 16 to 17 percent as Dell Computer Corp's unbridled growth continued and Hewlett-Packard Co had a surprising surge. International Data Corp, of Framingham, Mass., says the U.S. was the strongest with 19 percent growth, Asia/Pacific grew 14 percent, while Japan grew only six percent. Western Europe had better-than-expected growth of 11 percent.

TOKYO - Amid global concerns about greenhouse-gas emissions, Toyota Motor Corp is taking steps to market environmentally friendly "hybrid" cars, even though it expects the venture to register losses initially. Toyota says it plans to introduce the vehicles, which combine a gasoline engine and an electric motor, in Japan later this year.
BONN - Wine-drinkers in Britain, the Netherlands and Denmark helped boost German wine exports 4.7 percent to 2.3 million hectolitres in 1996, the ZMP farm price and marketing office says.
